description.narrative:
Center for Global Development (CGD) is an independent, nonpartisan research institution founded in 2001. In addition to the headquarter in Washington, CGD has an office in London, CGD Europe, Cooperation partner for the contribution. CGD works to reduce global poverty and improve lives through innovative economic research that drives better policy and practice by the world's top decision makers. CGD's scholars conduct rigorous, impartial analysis, informed by evidence and experts from around the world.
The intervention will support parts of CGD's ongoing research programmes with focus on three key research themes; 1. Aid effectiveness and aid channels and partners 2. Development finance 3. Technology and new paths to development

Center for Global Development (CGD) är ett oberoende, icke-politiskt forskningsinstitut grundat 2001. Utöver huvudkontoret i Washington har CGD ett kontor i London, CGD Europe, avtalspart för insatsen. CGD arbetar för att minska global fattigdom och förbättra livsförhållanden genom innovativ ekonomisk forskning som driver bättre policy och beslutsfattande av världens främsta ledare. CGD:s forskare bedriver rigorös forskning, oberoende analys, baserad på bevis och experter från runtom i världen.
Insatsen kommer att stötta delar CGD:s pågående forskningsprogram med fokus på tre forskningsområden; 1. Biståndseffektvitet och biståndskanaler och partners 2. Utvecklingsfinansiering 3. Teknologi och nya vägar till utveckling

The intervention will support CGD's ongoing research programmes in three key research themes; 1. Aid effectiveness and aid channels and partners 2. Development finance 3. Technology and new paths to development The key outputs in terms of events and reports will be defined in annual work plans. Furthermore, there is built-in flexibility to each topic to allow CGD to react to events as they happen and respond to any shifting priorities in the political landscape. Throughout the partnership, CGD will also act as an independent convener for events to share and discuss core issues with key policy and decision-making audiences. These activities all have an overarching aim of building on and disseminating relevant and insightful evidence for effective development policy and practice to influential policy- and decision-makers.

description.narrative:
Workstream 1 Aid effectiveness and aid channels and partners: •The European Development Policy and Leadership program (EDPL) focused on informing EU leaderships efforts to create a cohesive and coordinated development finance system focused on effective investments and encouraging official development agencies and multilateral institutions to improve the scope and effectiveness of their climate finance. •CGD released updated versions of two flagship products on benchmarking development effectiveness: the fifth edition of the Quality of Official Development Assistance tool (QuODA) and the 2021 Commitment to Development Index (CDI).
Workstream 2 Financing for Development: •The Sustainable Development Finance (SDF) program focused their efforts on four primary workstreams: positioning the IMF as a leader in financing the transition to a green and equitable economy; increasing international cooperation in financing the COVID-19 recovery and sustainable transition of fragile states; positioning the multilateral development banks (MDBS) and development finance institutions to better meet development finance needs (while shifting towards a focus on global public goods); and continuing to provide thought leadership on key dimensions of bilateral aid and finance for the US and China.
Workstream 3 New Technology and Paths to Development: •CGDs Technology program continued to focus on the growing role of data and digital tools. •Work on the Governing Data for Development project highlighted the importance of having rules that govern how different actors can use personal data that protect citizens from harm while supporting useful innovation. •Three private roundtables aimed at identifying the challenges that LMICs face in establishing effective data governance frameworks and how to create a level playing field for digital trade that does not disadvantage poorer countries were held. •In December, the team published a summary of the projects work so far as well as and an article in the OECDs 2021 Development Cooperation Report on Why Data Protection Matters for Economic Development and How to Create a More Level Playing Field.
Development Leaders Conference: •For the second year in a row, CGD and Sida co-hosted the annual Development Leaders Conference. This two-day virtual conference convened bilateral and multilateral donors from across the globe for frank, peer-to-peer conversations on financing global public goods (GPGs) and leveraging private flows through blended finance. •The Development Leaders Conference has become a more established event in the annual calendar of development agency leaders. Attendance in 2021 was much more uniformly at the DG/Agency Head level and format is being honed to maximize frank exchanges rather than prepared interventions.
External Engagement: •CGD's website, including blogs and publications, received nearly 4 million pageviews in 2021. • Total event registrations have also doubled since 2020 with over 250,000 people from countries on every continent. •CGD's work was featured widely across major newspaper, radio, and TV outlets. Repeat coverage in major media outlets - including the BBC, Wall Street Journal, New York Times, Washington Post, Economist, Financial Times, Guardian, Reuters, USA TODAY, CNN, MSNBC, National Public Radio, and Radio Free Europe - led to pick up in other countries including, among others, South Africa, China, Germany, India, and Brazil.
